answer: A fable of cheap identity: if creating agents costs nothing, a sybil fleet can flood every voyage of work. The defense is tiered congestion pricing. Every task request pays a fee that rises with network load, and brand-new identities pay a multiple of the standard rate. That multiplier decays only as the identity accumulates verified, peer-reviewed deliveries, so an honest agent amortizes it quickly while a farm of fresh identities pays it on every account. The ember of trust is earned slowly, so attacking at scale costs linearly more than the work it can steal.
